summary: The SAFE STEPS for Veterans Act of 2025 addresses mobility, aging care, and falls prevention services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs. It establishes a new Office of Falls Prevention within the Veterans Health Administration, creates new training and technology access rules for health care providers, requires specific falls risk assessments by physical or occupational therapists for certain veterans, and sets up reporting and research initiatives regarding home modifications and safety.

affected_groups.effect: They receive increased access to falls prevention education, assessments by physical or occupational therapists, enhanced safety technology in VA facilities, and potential pilot programs for home modifications.
affected_groups.group: Veterans, particularly older veterans or those at risk for falls

affected_groups.effect: They are subject to new training requirements for safe patient handling, mobility policies, and updated standards of care overseen by the new Office of Falls Prevention.
affected_groups.group: Department of Veterans Affairs health care providers and staff

key_provisions: Establishes an Office of Falls Prevention within the Veterans Health Administration, led by a Chief Officer of Falls Prevention, to oversee, evaluate, and improve falls prevention health care services.
Requires the Chief Officer to oversee a national public education campaign and award grants for local education campaigns aimed at reducing falls and increasing awareness of available VA benefits.
Expands the Interagency Coordinating Committee on Healthy Aging and Age-Friendly Communities to include the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

Requires the VA to issue or update directives for safe patient handling and mobility, including biennial training for providers and ensuring access to appropriate technology in medical and emergency settings.
Directs the VA to determine the feasibility and advisability of a pilot program providing home improvements and structural alterations to prevent falls for eligible veterans.

Mandates that licensed physical or occupational therapists conduct falls risk assessments and provide prevention services for certain individuals in VA nursing homes or receiving extended care services.
missing_information: The total authorized funding or budgetary cost for establishing the Office of Falls Prevention, grants, and pilot programs is not specified in the text.
Specific details on the exact criteria or locations for the potential home modification pilot program are not finalized, as the Secretary must first determine its feasibility and advisability.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The SAFE STEPS for Veterans Act of 2025 addresses mobility, aging care, and falls prevention services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs. It establishes a new Office of Falls Prevention within the Veterans Health Administration, creates new training and technology access rules for health care providers, requires specific falls risk assessments by physical or occupational therapists for certain veterans, and sets up reporting and research initiatives regarding home modifications and safety.
summary_detail.significance: This bill directs structural and administrative changes within the Department of Veterans Affairs focused entirely on veteran mobility and fall reduction. Its significance lies in creating dedicated leadership, standardized training, mandatory professional assessments, and research programs targeted at lowering fall rates and improving aging care services for veterans.
